purpose: Keep ZONES candidate scores, source-derived seeds, solar-error metrics, map packets, and adoption material from becoming time-zone recommendations, national baselines, or whole-policy objectives without the required civic evidence and reviews.

pitfalls.boundary: Candidate scores, map packets, comparison tables, moved-population metrics, and generated packet indexes are measurement evidence only while the recommendation gate is closed; they are not preferred, best, ready-to-adopt, or public-policy advice.

The four-county source-derived seed, boundary-backed local maps, and exploratory national visual packets are smoke or visual-inspection evidence only; they are not a national current-law baseline, legal-assignment scorecard, or complete source-ready dataset.

Solar-time fit is one measurement axis; candidate comparisons must keep convenience of commerce, disruption, public preference, legal process, implementation cost, source completeness, and review status visible.
